chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abu Nahshal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

If goodness (charity/kindness) were to flow upon eighty palms (i.e., be distributed through eighty people), all of them would be recompensed for it, without the original donor having anything of his reward diminished.
ai.seo_question: Does distributing charity through others reduce the donor's reward?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni cites this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the mechanism of shared reward (*shirkat al-ajr*) in charity, emphasizing that the donor's share is not diminished by the number of intermediaries. This principle underscores the multiplicative nature of good deeds in Shia jurisprudence, where each participant in the chain of distribution—from the giver to the final recipient—receives full, independent recompense for their specific role.
